claims.claim: The forever loop is an event-based background loop that yields to other code; you cannot use break or continue inside it (unlike for/while loops).
show string scrolls text left on the LED screen if it is larger than the screen; it takes an optional interval parameter (milliseconds) that controls scroll speed.
show icon displays a named icon and has an optional interval parameter whose default display time is 600 milliseconds.
pause(ms) pauses the program for the given number of milliseconds (1000 ms = 1 s); if ms is NaN the pause defaults to 20 ms.
The if block runs its inner code only when the boolean condition is true; else and else if branches are added via the + symbol, so if/then/else is conditional, not sequential.
on gesture (input.onGesture) is an event handler that runs code when a gesture occurs; the gesture parameter includes shake, logo up/down, screen up/down, tilt left/right, free fall, 3g, and 6g.
The pick random block returns a pseudo-random integer inclusive of both the min and max bounds; Math.randomRange is deprecated in favor of randint.

input.acceleration(dimension) returns acceleration in milli-g (1/1000 of a g); dimensions are X (left/right), Y (forward/back), Z (up/down), and Strength (combined). When flat with screen up, x=0, y=0, z=-1023, strength=1023.
